of parents and children from sexual intercourse with one another, the second

summary: Early human social organization evolved through successive taboos on inbreeding, first excluding parents and children, and then brothers and sisters from mating.
context: Engels traces the biological and social drivers of early family structures. As communities prohibited marriage between close relatives, tribal groups organized into distinct clans (gentes) that required marrying outside the clan.
